chunks: “The wives of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله did not make up the salat when they menstruated. However, when the time of salat entered, they would use cotton, perform wudu (ablution), then sit near the mosque and remember Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

key_terms.النَّبِيِّ: the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.فَيَذْكُرْنَ: then they remember Allah through dhikr
key_terms.لَا يَقْضِينَ: they do not make up or perform as qada'
key_terms.نِسَاءُ: the women, here referring to the wives
key_terms.يَتَحَشَّيْنَ: they use cotton or take hygienic precaution

ai.seo_question: Do menstruating women make up prayers, and what should they do at prayer time?
ai.summary: This hadith states that menstruating women do not make up missed salat. It also describes a recommended devotional practice during the prayer time: preparing oneself, performing wudu (ablution), and engaging in dhikr near the mosque.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.206 – (From Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)), He said:

'The wives of the Prophet did not make up the prayers when they were menstruating. However, when the time for prayer entered, they would use cotton (for cleanliness), perform wudu (ablution), and then sit near the mosque to remember Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic.'
